sentences.text: Opisthocoelicaudia skarzynskii is a genus of dinosaur.
This animal measured approximately 11.4 to 13 meters in length, featuring a small head, a very long neck, a barrel-shaped trunk, and four column-like legs.
Its specific name refers to the concave posterior sides of its anterior tail vertebrae.
Maria Magdalena Borsuk-Białynicka named and described the species in 1977 after a well-preserved skeleton was unearthed in 1965.
Fossils were found in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia, where only two additional incomplete specimens are known besides the type specimen.
Researchers propose that the dinosaur could rear on its hind legs based on skeletal features, though bite marks on the type specimen indicate predators fed on the carcass.
Borsuk-Białynicka originally assumed the neck was horizontal or slightly slanted downward, while later work in 2007 suggested the back dipped towards the rear.
It is currently classified as a derived member of the Titanosauria, having been originally placed within the family Camarasauridae.
Opisthocoelicaudia lived during the Late Cretaceous Period in the Nemegt Formation, an environment whose exact age remains unknown due to a lack of radiometric dating.

The exact relationships within Titanosauria are debated, with some suggesting it might be closely related to Alamosaurus or even the same species as Nemegtosaurus due to the lack of a known skull. Upchurch and colleagues argued in 2004 that Alamosaurus is not related to Opisthocoelicaudia and should be placed outside the Saltasauridae, while others debate whether these genera form a monophyletic group called Opisthocoelicaudiinae or if this group is paraphyletic.
